answer:
Verdict: no

## What the trace shows

Across the whole trace (0–30,612 ms), PID 664605 (`jobrunner`) **exited normally with status 0** at about 30,099.6 ms—roughly 0.5 seconds before the trace ended. Its shutdown after the last run of its work threads took about 0.1 ms.

## What it was doing before it exited

The main `jobrunner` thread spent 98.7% of its time in timer sleeps, waking the `job-0` through `job-3` threads. Those workers ran about 5.5% of the time each and spent about 94.4% waiting on futex condition waits. The main thread also spent about 255 ms waiting for child processes. The `watchdog` thread was idle and never woke to do work.

The trace shows a normal exit, not a process left running at the end. It cannot establish what the program considered “done.”
